# Recorded GUI reference workflows

The indicator recorder observes the actual status widget while a recorded turn frees
a coefficient, performs an adopted native fit and inspects its result. Peer barriers
hold the turn before actions, between an action and the fit, after adoption and before
completion. Pointer and native-fit signals supplement periodic rendered-state samples.
A separate run hides the real indicator at an intermediate barrier and restores it
before the final hold; the same validator must reject that trace. No model is called.

The retained trace is read after completion, with explicit final-held, final-response
delivered-but-still-active and terminal observations in order. A second response barrier
separates final-message delivery from the turn-completed notification. The completion-loss
control hides the indicator only in that suffix while leaving the earlier final hold
correct; the same throughout-turn validator must reject it.

The skill fixture transcribes the current guide's fourteen ordered GUI annotations
into distinct creation, file and web routes. The route actions come from the guide,
never from the app's available object names. Removing annotations fails closed. Intake
guides explicitly delegate GUI operations to the shared route guide and are each
replayed separately. The fitting guide's explicit GUI step shows Assistant before
asking; scientific decision loops are not represented as fixed click sequences.

Each skill has a nonempty workflow inventory. Every input target must be visible,
enabled and actually reachable before the driver sends input. Creation must add an
object, file routes must show the ordinary chooser and load authored rows or a site,
and web routes must open their source chooser, execute Search and expose actual results.
Fresh route projects prevent a prior route from satisfying the next route's postcondition.
The current app requires a structure before enabling the Experiment page; that setup
uses ordinary Create controls and leaves experiments empty for the Create-first check.

The CIF, three measured rows, full experiment and collection digests are authored here.
Their values are not copied from an implementation result. They prove GUI input flow,
not scientific fit quality. Missing, disabled and reordered targets go through the same
running-app workflow; their controls require refusal at the intended target, so an
unrelated setup failure cannot count as a successful fault control.
